reader.requirement: At --std 85, THRU and THROUGH are interchangeable spellings wherever the data description entry's formats use them: the format-2 RENAMES ... THROUGH/THRU data-name-3 and the format-3 condition-name VALUE literal-1 THROUGH/THRU literal-2 ranges, with identical meaning.
reader.edition-search: BindRenames (DataBinder.cs:3070) sets thru = rc.THRU() is not null || rc.THROUGH() is not null and never asks the edition; the renamesClause rule is (THRU | THROUGH) with no predicate; THRU and THROUGH are plain lexer tokens reserved at every edition. Grepped BindRenames and the two grammar rules for Edition/DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry: none.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1_renames_through_thru covers the RENAMES spelling pair; the level-88 VALUE THRU/THROUGH range half of format 3 is not exercised

probes.printed: R1=[ABCD] R2=[ABCD] R3=[CD] / R1=[WXYZ] C=[EF] / LOW1 / LOW2 / HI1 / NOT LOW2 / HI1 AT 10
probes.expected: THRU and THROUGH RENAMES name the same area; 88 VALUE ranges with either word behave alike, including a mixed VALUES ARE 10 THRU 20, 50 THROUGH 60 list
refused: no other spelling is equivalent

probes.printed: error COBOL2740: 'R1' RENAMES WB THRU WA: the beginning of data-name-3 precedes the beginning of data-name-2
probes.expected: THROUGH carries the same range rules as THRU (refused)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.3.3 SR4  (5.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4

reader.notes: Both words are distinct tokens and every consumer tests the pair together, so the spelling cannot change meaning. A cosmetic point: COBOL2740 echoes THRU when the source wrote THROUGH.

refuter.evidence: Probe r2thru --std 85: 66 RG1 RENAMES A THROUGH B (group end) and RG2 RENAMES B1 THRU C print [ABCD][CDE]; 88 alphanumeric ranges VALUE "A" THROUGH "F" vs VALUES "A" THRU "F" "K" THROUGH "N" with L='M' give NOT L1 / L2; LOW-VALUE THROUGH "B" gives NOT L3; negative ranges -10 THROUGH -1 and -10 THRU -1 both true for -5; SET L2 TO TRUE stores 'A'. Both spellings behave identically in formats 2 and 3. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.5.3.3 SR4  (5.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR4'.
